required_outcomes: Recognises the tenant's 17 March email as withdrawing the request: their household has cleared the rubbish and builders' waste, and they no longer want levelling or gravel.

Stands down the contractor route being arranged through Oakley (no visit, no quote needed) and tells the landlord (Jenkins) in writing that the tenant has cleared the garden and withdrawn the request, so no decision is needed from him.
Acknowledges the tenant's email in writing and confirms that the request is being closed and nobody will attend.
Closes or cancels the request with no payment, recording the reason (withdrawn by the tenant after clearing the garden themselves).
acceptable_alternatives: Asking the tenant one quick confirmation before closing (for example that nothing is left in the garden), provided the contractor route is stood down and the landlord is told.
Keeping the request open with a short dated follow-up until the landlord acknowledges, instead of closing straight away.
positive_behaviours: Thanks the tenant and apologises for the wait since 17 January.
Suggests to the landlord that the garden can be looked at during the next routine inspection, with no charge to anyone.
Leaves any question of the tenant's van or tip costs to the landlord rather than promising or refusing reimbursement.
red_flags: Escalating to a human over a withdrawn request.
Continuing to chase the landlord for approval of the clearance as if the job were still live.
prohibited_actions: Booking or instructing a contractor to attend the garden.
Telling the tenant they will be reimbursed for the van or tip costs, or asking them to pay anything.
critical_failures: Sending a contractor or approving clearance spend after the tenant has withdrawn the request.
